subject.title: perf(publication): prevent historical FIFO cleanup from delaying current exact-review results

question: Should publication batches reserve two of eight slots for current authoritative candidates within a 15-minute recency window, with the remainder continuing historical FIFO cleanup?
rationale: The implementation can preserve existing correctness fences, but the service-share and recency threshold are operational product policy choices that determine the trade-off between current-result visibility and backlog drain.

options.title: Adopt the proposed bounded reservation
options.body: Land the two-of-eight, 15-minute policy with the documented feature-flag rollback and production telemetry gates.

options.title: Choose different fairness bounds
options.body: Keep the same fenced two-lane design but set a different reservation or recency window after defining the desired latency and backlog targets.

options.title: Retain strict FIFO
options.body: Do not add a freshness lane and accept historical-first admission until a different publication scheduling design is approved.

recommendation.title: Adopt the proposed bounded reservation
recommendation.body: Land the two-of-eight, 15-minute policy with the documented feature-flag rollback and production telemetry gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The related RFC identifies the publication coordination direction and this decision spans the broader queue architecture rather than a mechanical bug fix.
